metadata.title: Public Key Infrastructure

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for establishing, validating, and revoking cryptographic trust relationships using asymmetric key infrastructure.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Certificate authorities, registration authorities, certificate repositories, revocation services, and trust validation mechanisms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Constraint pattern governing cryptographic identity validation, certificate lifecycle management, and trust establishment.

props.name: depends-on-pattern
props.remarks: PKI relies on key management for secure generation, protection, rotation, and destruction of asymmetric keys.

props.name: depends-on-pattern
props.remarks: PKI enforces trust relationships for systems and identities responsible for institutional data.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Public Key Infrastructure aligns with NIST SP 800-32 guidance on PKI design and deployment.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: PKI supports TLS certificate issuance and validation consistent with NIST SP 800-52.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: PKI aligns with NIST SP 800-53 controls governing identity proofing, cryptographic mechanisms, and key management.

metadata.remarks: Public Key Infrastructure defines enforceable requirements for establishing and validating cryptographic trust across systems, services, and identities. This pattern governs certificate issuance, validation, and revocation, enabling secure authentication and encrypted communications while relying on Key Management for underlying key lifecycle assurance.

components.title: Certificate Authority Trust
components.description: Ensures certificate authorities are securely operated, trusted, and governed to issue valid digital certificates.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Compromise of certificate authority credentials or signing processes.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Hardened CA operations and protected signing keys preserve trust.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Cryptographic mechanisms support authentication using digital certificates.

components.title: Certificate Issuance and Identity Binding
components.description: Binds cryptographic certificates to verified identities, systems, or services.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Use of valid certificates issued without proper identity validation.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Strong identity proofing during certificate issuance prevents misuse.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Certificates are issued only to authenticated and authorized entities.

components.title: Certificate Validation
components.description: Validates digital certificates prior to trust decisions or cryptographic use.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Use of expired, revoked, or untrusted certificates.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Certificate path validation and revocation checking prevent misuse.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Cryptographic mechanisms validate peer identity before data transmission.

components.title: Certificate Revocation and Status Management
components.description: Ensures compromised or invalid certificates are revoked and no longer trusted.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Continued trust in revoked or compromised certificates.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Timely revocation and status publication prevent ongoing misuse.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Keying material and certificates are revoked when compromise is suspected.
